text:
elaine-support: Heads-up — Acme reports sudden mTLS handshake failures to our Private control plane (private-controlplane.redwood:443) after they rolled a network proxy update. Customer sees repeated TLS alerts and our control plane logs show connection resets. Can anyone pick this up?

raj-eng: On it. Do we have customer-side captures or at least the exact TLS alert code from their proxy? Also, which control plane VIP/IP are they hitting?

elaine-support: They hit 10.248.5.12 (VPC egress NAT). Their proxy logs: "TLS Alert 40 (handshake_failure)" and repeated "alert: unknown CA" earlier but customer says certs are fine. They ran a quick openssl check and got: 
```
$ openssl s_client -connect private-controlplane.redwood:443 -servername private-controlplane.redwood
CONNECTED(00000003)
139832...:error:14094410:SSL routines:ssl3_read_bytes:sslv3 alert handshake failure:s3_pkt.c:1493:SSL alert number 40
```

liam-sre: Do they have any middleboxes doing TLS inspection (SSL forward proxy) or HTTP proxy that could be terminating/re-signing? That often causes SNI or ALPN mismatches. Also ask for a tcpdump of the ClientHello from the customer egress so we can verify SNI and extensions.

elaine-support: Customer confirmed they enabled a new NGFW rule (SSL Forward Proxy) as part of the update. They just captured a short tcpdump showing the first 3 packets from the flow. Posting sanitized dump: 
```
08:42:15.123456 IP 198.51.100.22.55555 > 10.248.5.12.443: Flags [S], seq 0, win 64240, options [mss 1460,sackOK,TS val 123456 ecr 0,nop,wscale 7], length 0
08:42:15.123457 IP 198.51.100.22.55555 > 10.248.5.12.443: Flags [P.], seq 1:517, ack 1, win 64240, length 516
    0x0000:  16030102 02... (ClientHello fragmented/truncated in the middle of extensions)
08:42:15.123458 IP 10.248.5.12.443 > 198.51.100.22.55555: Flags [R.], seq 0, ack 517, win 0, length 0
```

raj-eng: Interesting — ClientHello length ~ 0x202 (514) and we see fragment/truncation. Many TLS proxies will munge or truncate large ClientHello with lots of extensions (ALPN, SNI, keyshare). If the proxy inspects and re-injects, it may drop unknown extensions used by modern TLS1.3 or filter keyshare groups -> handshake failure. Also check if the proxy does TCP MSS clamping or chops packets causing reassembly issues.

liam-sre: Quick checks to ask customer: 
- Are they doing SSL Forward Proxy with re-signing? If so, is our control-plane hostname on an allowlist to bypass inspection?
- Can they capture the *server-side* capture (on their egress) to confirm whether the ClientHello that reaches our IP has SNI set?
- Disable features like "drop-split-fragments" or set reassembly options temporarily.

elaine-support: They replied: Palo Alto SSL Forward Proxy enabled, no bypass rules for our control plane. They can add a bypass for the control-plane FQDN or IP, but asked if we have a recommended tcp/ip or iptables workaround while they test.

raj-eng: Workarounds: 
- Best: Bypass TLS inspection for private-controlplane.redwood (by IP or hostname) so original ClientHello passes through untouched.
- If bypass not possible: ensure proxy allows TLS1.3 keyshare and ALPN extensions, or upgrade the proxy cert profile to not strip unknown extensions.
- On edge NAT devices, clamp MSS to PMTU to avoid fragmentation-related truncation: 
```
# linux iptables mss clamp example (if they control the NAT box)
sudo iptables -t mangle -A POSTROUTING -p tcp --tcp-flags SYN,RST SYN -j TCPMSS --clamp-mss-to-pmtu
```

liam-sre: Also check for TCP segmentation offload (TSO/GSO) interactions on the firewall. Some NGFWs mis-handle large segmented client hello packets and send only the first segment to the server, causing malformed handshake. Disabling TSO or enabling reassembly fixes that in many cases.

elaine-support: Customer applied a bypass for 10.248.5.12 and retried — they say TLS handshake succeeds now. They also toggled the Palo Alto "packet buffer protection" setting and that also seemed to help.

raj-eng: Great, so root cause = SSL Forward Proxy + fragment/truncation/reassembly bug causing ClientHello mutilation. Recommend they keep bypass for control-plane FQDNs or update NGFW firmware/inspection profile. I'll draft KB steps.

liam-sre: From our side, we should log a note in the customer record and add a short troubleshooting checklist for mTLS failures caused by TLS inspection (SNI/ALPN/keyshare stripping, MSS/clamping, TSO). Also consider adding a control-plane health-check route on a fallback port we advertise for troubleshooting, but only with auth considerations.

deploy-bot: [alert] 1899991234 — support thread created for mTLS handshake failure (escalation). Ticket #INC-2026-542 created.

elaine-support: Thanks team — passing the KB + recommended config to Acme. Marking this thread resolved once they confirm GA traffic stable. :white_check_mark:
